from.place: Lemma 05SA(2): values of LF are functorial on morphisms

title: Left derived values are functorial
statement: In Situation 05S8 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of $\mathcal D$ such that $LF$ is defined at $X$ and at $Y$. Then there is a unique morphism $LF(f):LF(X)\to LF(Y)$ between the values such that for every commutative square $f\circ s=s'\circ f'$ with $s:X'\to X$ and $s':Y'\to Y$ in $S$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, the diagram formed by $LF(X)\to F(X')\to F(X)$, $LF(Y)\to F(Y')\to F(Y)$ (the first arrows being the cone maps of the essentially constant pro-objects) and the vertical maps $LF(f)$, $F(f')$, $F(f)$ commutes.

proof.text: For each object Z equal to X or Y, apply the pointwise Kan-extension bridge to the essentially constant pro-object defining LF(Z). It supplies a limit cone with vertex LF(Z) over the structured-arrow diagram (QZ $\downarrow$ Q), and its projection at every denominator object (Z', Q(s)^{-1}) is the cone map u_s:LF(Z)\to F(Z') for s:Z'\to Z in S.

source.place: Definition 05S9 and Lemma 05SA(2), in the pointwise Kan-extension reformulation

proof.text: The morphism Q(f):Q(X)\to Q(Y) induces a functor (Q(Y) \downarrow Q)\to(Q(X) \downarrow Q) by precomposition: (Z',\varphi:Q(Y)\to Q(Z')) is sent to (Z',\varphi\circ Q(f)). Restricting the limit cone for LF(X) along this functor gives a cone over the diagram defining LF(Y), so the universal property of the limit gives a unique morphism LF(f):LF(X)\to LF(Y) whose component at (Z',\varphi) is the LF(X)-cone projection at (Z',\varphi\circ Q(f)).

source.place: Lemma 05SA(2), construction of the morphism from the universal property of the (cofiltered) limit

proof.text: For a commutative denominator square f\circ s=s'\circ f' with s:X'\to X and s':Y'\to Y in S, the denominator object (Y',Q(s')^{-1}) is sent by precomposition to (Y',Q(s')^{-1}\circ Q(f)) in (Q(X) \downarrow Q), and Q(s')^{-1}\circ Q(f)=Q(f')\circ Q(s)^{-1} because Q(f)\circ Q(s)=Q(s')\circ Q(f'). Hence f' is a morphism (X',Q(s)^{-1})\to(Y',Q(s')^{-1}\circ Q(f)) of (Q(X) \downarrow Q), and naturality of the LF(X)-cone together with the projection formula from Step 1 gives u_{s'}\circ LF(f)=F(f')\circ u_s; composing with F(s') and using f\circ s=s'\circ f' gives the required commutative diagram through F(X) and F(Y).

source.place: Lemma 05SA(2), comparison diagram for a commutative square with denominators in S

proof.text: For any (Z',\varphi:Q(Y)\to Q(Z')), the localization Hom-colimit bijection represents \varphi as Q(g)\circ Q(s')^{-1} for some s':W\to Y in S and g:W\to Z'. By the right-multiplicative-system axiom (RMS2), applied to f:X\to Y and s':W\to Y, choose t:V\to X in S and f':V\to W with f\circ t=s'\circ f'. Thus the denominator-square property gives u_{s'}\circ h=F(f')\circ u_t for either candidate h:LF(X)\to LF(Y). The limit cone projection at (Z',\varphi) is F(g)\circ u_{s'} (by the bridge statement), so the composites of the two candidates with this projection agree. Since every structured-arrow object has such a denominator representation, all limit projections agree, and the limit universal property gives uniqueness.
